configuration_space_complete_basis: Three named ballast/keel options ('Deep draft', 'Shallow draft', 'Performance draft (hydraulic swing keel)') are positively evidenced (SRC-1), but no source states this is the complete materially relevant factory configuration space (e.g. market-specific variants, rig-only options unrelated to keel choice). configuration_space_complete is left False per the slice's explicit instruction not to infer completeness from the number of discovered configurations.
self_authorization_boundary_note: REVIEW amendment (review 5067543634): this file is a retained, editable research artifact, not a truth-authorizing one. scripts/search_oceanis_30_1.py's validate_oceanis_30_1_projection() independently re-derives design_id, configuration_space_complete, the exact configuration_id/named_variant_id set, every field's exact value, and every evidence_refs/configuration_evidence_refs entry against a hardcoded oracle before this file's content is permitted to become Search input -- it never trusts this file's own claims about itself. A field, value, evidence reference or completeness flag edited here without a matching independent-review amendment to that oracle fails admission rather than silently reaching Search.

deliberately_unresolved.reason: This keel is operator-adjustable between a shoal and a deep position (SRC-1's overall 'Draft Max 2.3 m' is the deepest bound across all three keel options, consistent with this configuration's deepest setting, but no source states one single factory-resolved draft value for this configuration -- it is inherently a continuous operator-controlled range, not a discrete factory alternative like the two fixed keels. Search's QualifiedNumericValue boundary carries exactly one confirmed value or none; inventing two synthetic 'raised'/'lowered' endpoint configurations from a page-level range is explicitly forbidden by the slice (Required Behavior B). This field is therefore left unresolved (MISSING) for this configuration rather than assigned any single number.

fields_deliberately_left_unresolved_desi.reason: SRC-1's spec-table 'Dry Weight 9,100 lbs / 4,120 kg' and SRC-1's separate marketing-prose 'a weight of 8,000 lbs' (TRAILERABLE section, same page) are not stated to share the same measurement basis, and neither is explicitly scoped to one specific keel option. SRC-6 (Finot-Conq) separately states 'Light displacement : 3,99 t' (3,990 kg) without keel-option scoping either. 3,990 kg sits on the opposite side of the Q3 threshold (>=4,000 kg) from 4,120 kg / 8,000 lbs (~3,629 kg), so this is a materially threshold-crossing discrepancy across sources whose applicability scope (which keel option, which measurement basis) cannot be positively established as identical. Per TECHNICAL_PROFILE_SPEC.v0.1.md section 5 (applicability before conflict) this cannot be responsibly forced into either a single CONFIRMED value or a same-scope UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT without inventing the missing scope information; it is left unresolved (MISSING) design-wide rather than bound to any one configuration.

SRC-1 describes 'self-tacking jib' and 'large overlapping genoa' as alternative headsail choices (never simultaneously), and Finot-Conq's own sail-plan drawing labels ('Deep draught keel - genoa', 'Deep draught keel - Foc autovireur [self-tacking jib]') reinforce a single-headsail-position architecture. This is consistent with a sloop rig, but no retrieved cleared source states the word 'sloop' (or an equivalent unambiguous single-mast-single-headsail-family declaration) outright. Consistent with the SLICE-0036 real-design validation precedent (research/validation/SL0036-marine-entailment-real-design-validation.md), inferring the controlled taxonomy token from single-headsail-position architecture rather than a literal source statement would be exactly the 'typical, not definitional' reasoning MARINE_TECHNICAL_ENTAILMENT.v0.1.md section 4 rule 1 forbids for cross-field entailment, and this research holds direct-field confirmation to the same literal-statement standard. Left MISSING design-wide.

No cleared source states an explicit masthead/fractional designation or a mast-fraction ratio (e.g. '9/10') for this design. SRC-4 (the pro.beneteauusa.com equipment-list PDF) did state 'Classic mast (Z-Diffusion) 9/10', which would have been strong direct evidence of a fractional rig, but SRC-4 is excluded from the evidence basis due to its robots.txt disallow (see source_retrieval_log.json). Left MISSING design-wide.

No cleared source states a controlled keel_type enum token (fin/bulb/long_fin/etc.) for either fixed-keel configuration; sources name the options by draft ('Deep draft'/'Shallow draft') and material is not stated in a cleared source either. Left MISSING for every configuration.

SRC-1 and SRC-5 both confirm 'twin rudders' (a direct rudder_count=2 fact, not itself projected into Search because no locked Q1-Q10 query needs rudder_count), but no cleared source states whether the twin rudders are skeg-supported or free-standing/spade. No skeg is mentioned in any cleared source, but per CLAUDE.md's core provenance guardrail absence of mention is never treated as negative evidence of an absent skeg. Left MISSING for every configuration.

SRC-1/SRC-5 describe cockpit layout and seating ('wonderfully big cockpit', 'two large benches') and a bow/aft two-cabin layout, but no cleared source states the controlled cockpit_position token ('aft'/'center'/'forward'/'multiple') outright. Left MISSING for every configuration.
